blocks.explanation:
Three sines minus the sine of their sum must become a product of three sines.
Plan: pair \(\sin\alpha + \sin\beta\) and \(\sin\gamma - \sin(\alpha + \beta + \gamma)\). Both pairs produce the factor \(\sin\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\); take it out and change the remaining difference of cosines into a product.
steps:
Given: L.H.S. \(= \sin\alpha + \sin\beta + \sin\gamma - \sin(\alpha + \beta + \gamma)\).
To prove: L.H.S. \(= 4\sin\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\sin\frac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\sin\frac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\).
Method: \(\sin P \pm \sin Q\) and \(\cos P - \cos Q\) formulas.

First pair
\[\sin\alpha + \sin\beta = 2\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\cos\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin P + \sin Q\) formula.

Second pair (\(P = \gamma\), \(Q = \alpha + \beta + \gamma\))
\[\dfrac{P + Q}{2} = \dfrac{\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma}{2}\]
\[\dfrac{P - Q}{2} = -\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\]
\[\sin\gamma - \sin(\alpha + \beta + \gamma)\]
\[= -2\cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma}{2}\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin P - \sin Q = 2\cos\frac{P + Q}{2}\sin\frac{P - Q}{2}\) and \(\sin(-u) = -\sin u\).

Take out the common factor
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\;\times\]
\[\left[\cos\tfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2} - \cos\tfrac{\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma}{2}\right]\]
Why: \(2\sin\frac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\) is in both pairs.

The bracket: \(\cos P - \cos Q\) with \(P = \frac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\), \(Q = \frac{\alpha + \beta + 2\gamma}{2}\)
\[\dfrac{P + Q}{2} = \dfrac{2\alpha + 2\gamma}{4} = \dfrac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\]
\[\dfrac{P - Q}{2} = \dfrac{-2\beta - 2\gamma}{4} = -\dfrac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\]
Why: Add and subtract the two angles carefully, then halve.

Change the bracket into a product
\[\cos P - \cos Q\]
\[= -2\sin\tfrac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\sin\left(-\tfrac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\right)\]
\[= 2\sin\tfrac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\sin\tfrac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\]
Why: \(\sin(-u) = -\sin u\), so the two minus signs cancel.

Put it back
\[\text{L.H.S.} = 2\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\;\times\]
\[2\sin\tfrac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\sin\tfrac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\]
\[= 4\sin\tfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\sin\tfrac{\beta + \gamma}{2}\sin\tfrac{\gamma + \alpha}{2}\]
\[= \text{R.H.S.}\]
Why: \(2 \times 2 = 4\); the order of the factors does not matter.
